title: CLIENT SATISFACTION SURVEY
intro:
This evaluation form aims to gather feedback on the quality of services provided by the office. The responses collected will help assess client satisfaction and identify areas for service improvement to ensure efficient, responsive, and client-centered service delivery.
Data Privacy Notice: The Mindanao State University General Santos values your privacy and is dedicated to protecting your personal data in compliance with the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (Republic Act No. 10173).
This Privacy Notice explains how we collect, use, process, store, and protect your personal information in relation to the Client Satisfaction Survey conducted by Office of Monitoring and Evaluation (OME) under the Office of the Vice Chancellor for Planning and Development of MSU-General Santos.

This survey aims to assess the quality of services provided by university offices and personnel, identify areas for improvement, and support the university’s commitment to transparency, accountability, and continuous service improvement.

notice.heading: Personal Data Collected and Manner of Collection
notice.body:
We collect information directly from you through this survey form, which may be administered physically or through digital platforms.

The information collected may include:

Optional Identifying Information
Name (optional)
Contact Information
Contact number
Email address
Demographic Information
Age
Gender
Client type (student, parent/guardian, faculty/staff, alumni, prospective student, visitor, or others)
Service-Related Information
Service availed from the university office
Name of the MSU-Gensan employee providing the service
Feedback and Evaluation Data
Ratings regarding service quality, fairness, courtesy, timeliness, facilities, and overall satisfaction
Suggestions or comments on how university services may be improved
Providing personal information in this survey is voluntary, and you may choose not to disclose optional details.

notice.heading: Basis, Use, and Purpose for Processing of Personal Data
notice.body:
The information you provide will be used for the following purposes:
To evaluate the quality and efficiency of services delivered by university offices
To identify strengths and areas for improvement in service delivery
To support institutional planning, monitoring, and decision-making
To comply with government performance monitoring requirements, including citizen/client satisfaction measurement systems
To enhance transparency, accountability, and public service delivery
Processing of your data is based on the following legal grounds under the Data Privacy Act of 2012:
Section 12(c) – processing necessary for the performance of public authority functions
Section 12(f) – processing necessary for legitimate institutional interests
Consent of the data subject, where applicable

notice.heading: Methods utilized for automated access:
notice.body:
If the survey is conducted through online platforms, certain technical information may be automatically recorded, such as:
Internet Protocol (IP) address
Device or browser type
Date and time of submission
These are collected solely to maintain system integrity, prevent misuse, and improve digital services.

notice.heading: Disclosure of Personal Data:
notice.body:
Your personal data will not be disclosed to unauthorized third parties.

Information may only be shared:
With authorized MSU-Gensan offices responsible for service quality evaluation and reporting
With government oversight bodies when required for performance monitoring and compliance reporting
When required by law or permitted under Sections 12 or 13 of the Data Privacy Act
Survey results will generally be reported in aggregated or anonymized form to ensure that individual respondents cannot be identified. All disclosures are governed by data sharing agreements or appropriate authority documentation.

notice.heading: Risks Involved:
notice.body: Risk refers to potential harm or danger to individuals or organizations. This can happen through unauthorized collection, use, disclosure, or access to personal data, affecting confidentiality, integrity, and availability. We ensure security measures to safeguard personal information, but absolute protection is not guaranteed, especially against cyberattacks or unauthorized access. However, we have policies in place to manage security incidents, which align with existing National Privacy Commission (NPC) policies, circulars, and other guidelines.

notice.heading: Data Protection and Security Measures:
notice.body:
We use reasonable and appropriate technical, physical, and organizational security measures to protect personal data from unauthorized disclosure, misuse, alteration, loss, or destruction. We implement the following mechanisms to protect your data:
Role-based access control and identity verification
Encrypted storage of digital files
Secure facilities for physical document storage
Data protection policies embedded in staff protocols
Annual privacy and security awareness training for Admission personnel

notice.heading: Storage, Retention, and Disposal:
notice.body:
Survey responses will be stored securely in university databases and records systems.

Your personal data will be retained for three (3) years from the date of collection to support institutional monitoring, reporting, and service improvement initiatives.

After the retention period, data will be securely disposed of through:
Secure deletion or anonymization of digital records
Shredding or destruction of physical documents
in accordance with MSU-Gensan’s records management policies and applicable laws.

notice.heading: Data Subject Rights:
notice.body:
Under the DPA, you have the following rights:
Right to be informed. You have the right to know how we collect, use, store, share, and dispose of your data. We share this information with you through our Privacy Notices.
Right to object. If the personal data processing involved is based on consent or legitimate interest.
Right of access. You have the right to request information about how we use, store, disclose, or protect your personal data.
Right to rectification. You have the right to request modifications or corrections to your personal data if it is inaccurate, outdated, or false.
Right to erasure or blocking. You have the right to request the deletion of your personal data or ask us to stop using your data for specific purposes.
Right to data portability. You have the right to request that we transfer your personal data to another organization or directly to you under certain circumstances.
Right to file a complaint and ask for damages. If you believe your rights as a data subject have been violated or if you have suffered damages due to any issues with your personal data, you can reach out to our Data Privacy Committee for assistance. If we cannot resolve your concerns or if you are unsatisfied with our response, you have the right to file a complaint with the NPC.
If you have privacy concerns, believe your personal data has been breached, feel your rights as a data subject have been violated, or wish to exercise your data subject rights, fill out our Data Subject Request (DSR) Form by contacting the Data Protection Officer.

notice.heading: Changes to the Privacy Notice:
notice.body: We reserve the right to update or revise this privacy notice at any time. We will issue a new privacy notice whenever there are significant changes. Previous versions of the privacy notice can be provided to data subjects upon request.

notice.heading: Feedback on our Privacy Notice:
notice.body:
If you have any suggestions, comments, or concerns about our privacy notice, or if you have questions about our data privacy practices, you can reach out to:

Assoc. Prof. Lumer Jude Doce, DIT
Data Protection Officer
dpo.msugensan@gmail.com
